configuration_scope: The named controls change only Writers, Values and MaxWriterRestarts as shown. GC={gc1}, EnableFix=TRUE, the six invariants, symmetry, Spec and deadlock setting are retained. All runs use the original module.
module_library: tlaplus/CommunityModules, 78b98ae9939d2fe7a6615e9a4b21dd6c23ef8ff3, modules directory; pinned jars for TLC
protocol: Small, Medium and original ran sequentially on one isolated host. The two single-parameter changes ran sequentially on a second host of the same shape with a 300 s budget per cell. Whole-process GNU time, fresh process per row, CPU affinity fixed, default clock. Small uses one worker; medium and original use eight. Core --compat=tlc --workers N --library-path MODULES --fp 0 --seed 0 --max-memory 18g --time-limit Ns --output json. Pinned TLC -Xmx12g -XX:+UseParallelGC -XX:ActiveProcessorCount=N -DTLA-Library=MODULES -cp TOOLS:COMMUNITY:DEPS tlc2.TLC -workers N -seed 0 -fp 0 -config CFG SlateDBWAL.tla. Time budget 240 s for controls, 180 s on original. TLC last progress is a sampled lower bound.

unbounded_discovery_comparison.scope: Two fingerprint searches, seed and polynomial 0. Equal counters do not independently establish collision-free state identities. TLC uses MSBDiskFPSet and DiskStateQueue.

The replay asserts all 23,269,077 membership decisions against the capture; 65,536 hot entries, 32,768 queries per window. This row counts buffered page loads in the standalone trace program.

Sequential processes on c7i.4xlarge. Page reads count buffered application reads, including cache hits. Write bytes accumulate over all sealed runs and merges.

resident_fingerprint_slots.question: Can ordinary resident membership save memory without truncating the engine's fingerprints?
resident_fingerprint_slots.host: Isolated r7i.8xlarge, us-east-1, Ubuntu 24.04; GNU time wall and maximum process RSS; trials sequential. Synthetic streams use one physical core, product checks use 16.
resident_fingerprint_slots.design: Keep full keys in small shards. From 4096 slots reconstruct the high byte from the shard and the low home bits from slot and displacement. Primary slots take six bytes at capacity bits 12..19, five at 20..27 and four at 28 or more. Full-key overflow handles displacements beyond 14. Rebuild the full existing fingerprint when growing a shard.
resident_fingerprint_slots.stream_recipe: mix(x) is the SplitMix64 finalizer: x=(x^(x>>30))*0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9; x=(x^(x>>27))*0x94d049bb133111eb; return x^(x>>31), all modulo 2^64. For i=1..N inclusive, insert mix(i) and verify contains(mix(i)); on every fourth i verify duplicate insert(mix(i/2)) and absent contains(mix(N+i)); check len=N, then contains(mix(i)) from 1 every 1031 keys through N. Both executables use dive_explore::Seen.
resident_fingerprint_slots.product_command: taskset -c 0-15 BINARY check MODULE --config CFG --library-path modules --workers 16 --compat=tlc --fp 0 --seed 0 --max-states N --max-memory 32g --time-limit 1000s --output json

one_shard_at_published_scale.host: Isolated r7i.8xlarge, us-east-1, Ubuntu 24.04; GNU time wall and maximum process RSS; trials sequential. Synthetic streams use one physical core, product checks use 16.
one_shard_at_published_scale.recipe: N=191406250 equals 49 billion divided by 256. Fix high byte 0x53, use the SplitMix64 finalizer in stream_recipe restricted to 56 bits after each multiplication, including its final xor-shift. For i=1..N insert each key. Every fourth i check contains and repeat insert for i/2 and check absence of N+i; then look up every inserted key and verify length. Final RSS comes from /proc/self/status after all lookups.
one_shard_at_published_scale.interpretation: One full-size shard at the mean occupancy of 256 uniformly populated shards at 49 billion fingerprints. This measures one shard in the actual resident implementation. A whole model has other shards, frontiers, values, predecessors and worker storage.

exact_membership_layout.platform: Dedicated EC2 r7i.8xlarge, 16 physical cores / 32 vCPUs, Xeon Platinum 8488C. Linux 7.0.0-1018-aws. Each run alone with CPU affinity 0-15.
exact_membership_layout.build: Rust 1.99.0, cargo build --locked --release -p dive-cli, LTO disabled, 16 codegen units. The bucket, inline and packed arms share the base and differ only in exact membership layout.

arm_definitions.bucket: Vector per distinct hash, separately owned state rows
arm_definitions.inline: First identity stored directly in each hash slot, separately owned state rows
arm_definitions.packed: Singleton hash slot, identities in lossless blocks of 256 rows, full equality for matching hashes

exact_membership_layout.command: dive check SlateDBWAL.tla --config OneValue.cfg --library-path modules --workers 16 --store exact --compat=tlc --fp 0 --seed 0 --max-memory 195g --time-limit 5500s --output json. Prefix trials add --max-states 10000000. Original trials use the released CFG, --max-memory 125g and --max-states 100000000.

released_configuration_completion.input: Unmodified released module and CFG, three writers, two values, one restart, fixed protocol, six invariants, configured symmetry, deadlocks disabled.
released_configuration_completion.platform: Dedicated EC2 r7i.48xlarge, 40 physical cores pinned, Xeon Platinum 8488C, 1536 GiB nominal. Core and pinned TLC run sequentially on this node.
released_configuration_completion.historical_comparison: The author reports roughly 49 billion unique states on the same constants. The released CFG enables symmetry. The reported run has no identified terminal log or checker version. Core exhausted this CFG at 4,910,385,789 fingerprints. Neither the tenfold difference nor a historical speedup is established. The notes, CFG and module were changed together at the pinned upstream revision.

earlier_protocol_with_fix.author_note: The author reports 49 billion unique states for the improved module and 12 billion for the simpler module at the same parameters. The archived SlateDBWAL_TLAPSBENCHBUG module and CFG actually specify four writers, one collector and two values; this protocol has no writer-restart parameter. The newer module and CFG use three writers and one restart. Both CFGs set EnableFix=TRUE. There is no final log or reported symmetry setting for the 12-billion figure.
earlier_protocol_with_fix.source_history: The 49B/12B comparison first occurs in the November 5 revision, which also published the separately named earlier protocol. The September and October examples predate that paragraph. The checked-in earlier protocol, rather than an inferred main-branch predecessor, supplies these experiments.
earlier_protocol_with_fix.host: EC2 r7i.16xlarge, Ohio, 32 physical cores; eight checker workers on the controls; process wall_s and peak_rss_kib from GNU time. Each checked all six supplied invariants using the supplied symmetry and deadlock setting.
earlier_protocol_with_fix.prepare: Copy the upstream .tla and .cfg for SlateDBWAL_TLAPSBENCHBUG unchanged. For W2 and W3, replace only {w1, w2, w3, w4} on the Writers line with {w1, w2} or {w1, w2, w3}. All measured configurations keep EnableFix=TRUE.
earlier_protocol_with_fix.core: dive check SlateDBWAL_TLAPSBENCHBUG.tla --config CFG --library-path MODULES --store exact --compat=tlc --workers 8 --seed 0 --fp 0 --time-limit 1200s --max-memory 420g --output json
earlier_protocol_with_fix.tlc: java -Xmx22g -XX:+UseParallelGC -XX:ActiveProcessorCount=8 -DTLA-Library=MODULES -cp ORACLE_AND_COMMUNITY_JARS tlc2.TLC -seed 0 -fp 0 -workers 8 -metadir SCRATCH -config CFG SlateDBWAL_TLAPSBENCHBUG.tla
